summary.intent: Use the GSD manager to orchestrate parallel phase work on cipher-box milestone v1.1, dispatching background plan/execute agents and inline discuss for phases 28-32.
summary.outcome: Before dispatching work, discovered stale worktrees and a merge conflict; cleaned up two stale worktrees (Phase 28 already merged as PR #382), merged main into the current branch (phase-31-structural-decomposition), and resolved ROADMAP.md conflict markers. Phase 29 PR #383 is open and mergeable.

repo: Phase 28 (Code Hygiene & Logging) was already merged via PR #382 before the session started, but its worktrees were still active.
Phase 29 (Infrastructure Hardening) has PR #383 open with checks green except one Linux Cargo check still running.
The milestone uses decimal phase numbering (e.g., 19.1, 19.2) for sub-phases.
Planning files (.planning/ROADMAP.md, phase plan files) are tracked in git and generate merge conflicts when multiple branches touch them concurrently.
The current working branch for Phase 31 (Structural Decomposition) was 11 commits ahead of main — all docs/planning commits.

code.finding: Progress table at bottom of ROADMAP.md had leftover conflict markers after the initial merge resolution; required a second fix commit.

workflow: Before dispatching background agents, it's worth checking active worktrees and open PRs to avoid duplicate work on already-merged phases.
Stale worktrees from completed/merged phases should be pruned before starting new background agents to avoid confusion.

When planning files are committed on feature branches, merging main creates conflicts in ROADMAP.md and phase plan files — resolved by keeping the executed versions from main for already-merged phases.
GSD background agents leave behind worktrees that persist after PR merge and need manual cleanup.

friction: Two stale worktrees were left behind from Phase 28 after its PR was already merged, requiring manual detection and removal.
